title: iOS 27
description: iOS 27 was unveiled at Apple's Worldwide Developers Conference on June 8, 2026, as the successor to iOS 26. Its headline feature is Siri AI, a rebuilt version of Siri built on generative AI models capable of holding natural, back-and-forth conversations. The update reached the public in September 2026 alongside the new iPhone lineup.

title: WWDC 26
description: WWDC 2026 was Apple's annual developer conference, kicking off on June 8, 2026 with the keynote where iOS 27, along with iPadOS 27, macOS Golden Gate, watchOS 27 and other platform updates were unveiled. It also marked Tim Cook's final keynote as Apple's CEO before handing the role to hardware engineering chief John Ternus.

title: Huavei Pura X MAX
description: The Huawei Pura X Max launched in China on April 20, 2026, alongside the Pura 90 series, introducing a new "wide foldable" book-style design with a broader 16:10 aspect ratio. It features a 7.7-inch inner display and a 5.4-inch outer OLED cover screen, powered by the Kirin 9030 Pro chipset.

title: Huavei Pura 90 PRO
description: The Huawei Pura 90 Pro launched in China on April 20, 2026, continuing the Pura series' signature triangular camera module in a new gradient finish. It's powered by the Kirin 9030S chip and features a 200-megapixel periscope telephoto lens.

title: iPhone 17e
description: Announced March 2, 2026, and released March 11, the iPhone 17e is Apple's budget model, priced at $599. It upgrades on the iPhone 16e with the A19 chip, the faster C1X modem, and — for the first time in this lineup — MagSafe wireless charging.

title: Samsung Galaxy S26 ULTRA
description: The Galaxy S26 Ultra was announced at Samsung's Unpacked event in San Francisco on February 25, 2026, going on sale March 11. Its standout feature is a new Privacy Display that can dim the screen from side angles, keeping onlookers from seeing what's on it, alongside the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 chip.

title: Oppo Find X9 Ultra
description: The Oppo Find X9 Ultra launched April 21, 2026, in China and select global markets as one of the year's most camera-focused flagships. It packs a quad-camera system with a 200-megapixel main sensor and a 200-megapixel periscope telephoto lens, powered by the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5.

title: Xiaomi 17 ULTRA
description: The Xiaomi 17 Ultra debuted in China on December 25, 2025, before its global launch in Barcelona on February 28, 2026, just ahead of Mobile World Congress. Built with Leica, it features a 1-inch main camera sensor and a 200-megapixel periscope telephoto lens.

title: Vivo X300s
description: The Vivo X300s launched in China on March 30, 2026, becoming the first phone in Vivo's X series with a 144Hz display. It also carries the largest battery yet in the lineup at 7,100mAh, alongside a 200-megapixel Zeiss-branded main camera.

title: Redmi K90 PRO MAX
description: Announced in October 2025 and released in China on October 23, the Redmi K90 Pro Max is the first "Pro Max" model in Redmi's K series. It pairs the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 chip with a periscope telephoto camera and a Bose-tuned loudspeaker.

title: Vivo X300 PRO
description: The Vivo X300 Pro was announced October 13 and released October 17, 2025, as the higher-end model in Vivo's X300 series. It runs on MediaTek's then-new Dimensity 9500 chip with a 6.78-inch LTPO OLED display reaching up to 4,500 nits of brightness.

title: Vivo X300
description: Launched alongside the Pro model on October 17, 2025, the standard Vivo X300 offers a more compact 6.31-inch display while sharing the same Dimensity 9500 chip as its bigger sibling.

title: Xiaomi 17
description: The standard Xiaomi 17 was unveiled in China on September 25, 2025, featuring a 6.3-inch flat OLED display and a large silicon-carbon battery rated at up to 7,000mAh. It reached global markets, including a Leica-branded camera system, in early 2026.

title: Oppo F31 Pro
description: Released in September 2025, the Oppo F31 Pro is a mid-range device built around a large 7,000mAh battery and the MediaTek Dimensity 7300 chip, aimed at buyers who prioritize battery life over flagship specs.

title: iPhone 17 PRO / 17 PRO MAX
description: The iPhone 17 Pro and Pro Max were unveiled at Apple's "Awe Dropping" event on September 9, 2025, alongside the standard iPhone 17 and the all-new iPhone Air. Pre-orders opened September 12, with devices arriving in stores on September 19, 2025.

title: iPhone Air
description: Introduced on September 9, 2025, the iPhone Air marked a brand-new category in Apple's lineup: the thinnest iPhone ever made, at just 5.6mm. Apple achieved this by moving internal components closer to the rear camera and removing the physical SIM card slot, while still promising all-day battery life.

title: iPhone 17
description: The iPhone 17 launched on September 19, 2025, as Apple's standard flagship model, featuring a larger 6.3-inch display with ProMotion support and an A19 chip. It was priced the same as its predecessor, the iPhone 16, despite the display and performance upgrades.

title: Vivo Y400
description: The Vivo Y400 5G launched in India on August 4, 2025, as a mid-range phone positioned in the sub-₹25,000 segment. It runs on the Snapdragon 4 Gen 2 chipset with a 6.67-inch AMOLED display and 120Hz refresh rate.

title: Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 7
description: Announced July 9, 2025, at Samsung's Unpacked event in Brooklyn and released July 25, the Galaxy Z Fold 7 became Samsung's thinnest and lightest book-style foldable to date. It was also the first Samsung foldable to feature a 200-megapixel main camera.

title: iOS 26
description: iOS 26 was announced at WWDC on June 9, 2025 and released to the public on September 15, 2025. It was the first iOS version to carry a year-based number instead of a sequential one, aligning it with macOS, watchOS and Apple's other platforms, and introduced the Liquid Glass design language.

title: iPhone 16e
description: Announced February 19, 2025 and released February 28, the iPhone 16e replaced the iPhone SE line as Apple's budget model, starting at $599. It brought the A18 chip and an edge-to-edge display, though it launched without MagSafe support.

title: Oppo A5 Pro
description: The Oppo A5 Pro launched internationally on February 25, 2025, as a budget-friendly model powered by the MediaTek Dimensity 6300 chip, with a 6.67-inch display and a starting price around €260.

title: iPhone 16 PRO / 16 PRO MAX
description: Unveiled at Apple's "Glowtime" event on September 9, 2024, the iPhone 16 Pro and Pro Max introduced the A18 Pro chip and a dedicated Camera Control button. They were the first iPhones built with Apple Intelligence in mind from the ground up.

title: iPhone 16 / 16 Plus
description: Launched alongside the Pro models on September 9, 2024, the iPhone 16 and 16 Plus brought the Camera Control button and a redesigned vertical camera layout enabling spatial photos and video to the standard lineup.

title: iOS 18
description: iOS 18 was announced at WWDC on June 10, 2024, and released September 16, 2024. It introduced Apple Intelligence, customizable Home Screen app icon colors, and a redesigned Control Center.

title: realme 12 Pro+
description: The realme 12 Pro+ was released January 29, 2024, positioned as a mid-range device with camera hardware that punched above its price class, part of realme's push to bring flagship-style photography features downmarket.

title: Pixel 8
description: Google unveiled the Pixel 8 at its Made by Google event in New York on October 4, 2023, with sales beginning October 12. It was the first Pixel to launch with a promise of seven years of OS and security updates, powered by Google's Tensor G3 chip.

title: iPhone 15 PRO / 15 PRO MAX
description: Announced September 12, 2023, the iPhone 15 Pro and Pro Max switched to a titanium frame, replaced the mute switch with the Action Button, and debuted the A17 Pro, Apple's first 3-nanometer chip.

title: iPhone 15 / 15 Plus
description: Released alongside the Pro models on September 12, 2023, the iPhone 15 and 15 Plus were the first standard iPhones to switch from Lightning to USB-C and to bring the Dynamic Island to the non-Pro lineup.

title: iOS 17
description: Announced at WWDC on June 5, 2023, and released September 18, 2023, iOS 17 introduced StandBy mode for bedside displays, Live Voicemail, and redesigned Contact Posters for calls.

title: iPhone 14 PRO / 14 PRO MAX
description: Unveiled September 7, 2022, the iPhone 14 Pro and Pro Max replaced the notch with the Dynamic Island, introduced an Always-On display, and upgraded to a 48-megapixel main camera.

title: iPhone 14 / 14 Plus
description: Launched September 7, 2022, the iPhone 14 and 14 Plus introduced Crash Detection and satellite-based Emergency SOS for areas without cellular coverage.

title: iOS 16
description: Announced at WWDC on June 6, 2022, and released September 12, 2022, iOS 16 let users fully customize the Lock Screen with widgets and multiple styles for the first time.

title: iPhone SE (3rd generation)
description: Released March 18, 2022, the third-generation iPhone SE kept the classic iPhone 8 design but added 5G support and the A15 Bionic chip, the same chip found in the iPhone 13.

title: iPhone 13 PRO / PRO MAX
description: Announced September 14, 2021, the iPhone 13 Pro and Pro Max brought a 120Hz ProMotion display to iPhone for the first time, along with a new Cinematic mode for video.

title: iPhone 13 / 13 Mini
description: Launched alongside the Pro models on September 14, 2021, the iPhone 13 and 13 Mini featured a smaller notch and the new A15 Bionic chip.

title: iOS 15
description: Announced at WWDC on June 7, 2021, and released September 20, 2021, iOS 15 introduced FaceTime SharePlay, redesigned notifications, and Focus modes for filtering distractions.

title: iPhone 12 PRO / 12 PRO MAX
description: Announced October 13, 2020, the iPhone 12 Pro and Pro Max were Apple's first 5G iPhones, adding a LiDAR scanner for improved AR and low-light autofocus, along with MagSafe magnetic accessories.

title: iPhone 12 / 12 Mini
description: Unveiled alongside the Pro models on October 13, 2020, the iPhone 12 and 12 Mini brought back the flat-edge design last seen on the iPhone 5 and added 5G connectivity.

title: iOS 14
description: Announced at WWDC on June 22, 2020, and released September 16, 2020, iOS 14 brought Home Screen widgets and the App Library to iPhone for the first time.

title: iPhone 11 PRO / PRO MAX
description: Launched September 10, 2019, the iPhone 11 Pro and Pro Max introduced Apple's first triple-camera system and a dedicated Night mode for low-light photography.

title: iPhone 11
description: Released September 10, 2019, the standard iPhone 11 added a second, ultra-wide camera lens and was powered by the A13 Bionic chip.

title: iOS 13
description: Announced at WWDC on June 3, 2019, and released September 19, 2019, iOS 13 introduced system-wide Dark Mode to iPhone for the first time.

title: iPhone XS / XS MAX
description: Announced September 12, 2018, the iPhone XS and XS Max carried forward the Face ID design introduced with the iPhone X, powered by the A12 Bionic chip and offering dual-SIM support.

title: iPhone XR
description: Launched alongside the XS models on September 12, 2018, the iPhone XR offered the Face ID design at a lower price with an LCD "Liquid Retina" display and a wider range of colors.

title: iOS 12
description: Announced at WWDC on June 4, 2018, and released September 17, 2018, iOS 12 introduced Screen Time for tracking app usage and Memoji, animated personal avatars.

title: iPhone X
description: Released to mark the iPhone's 10th anniversary on September 12, 2017, the iPhone X removed the Home button entirely, introducing Face ID and an edge-to-edge OLED display for the first time.

title: iPhone 8 / 8 Plus
description: Launched the same day as the iPhone X, September 12, 2017, the iPhone 8 and 8 Plus kept the classic Home button design but switched to a glass back, enabling wireless charging for the first time on iPhone.

title: iOS 11
description: Announced at WWDC on June 5, 2017, and released September 19, 2017, iOS 11 redesigned the App Store and Control Center and brought drag-and-drop multitasking to iPad.

title: iOS 11 Flower
description: "Flower" is one of the built-in stock wallpaper categories Apple shipped with iOS 11, featuring close-up floral photography as an alternative to the system's default abstract wallpapers.

title: iOS 11 Retro Rainbow
description: "Retro Rainbow" is a stock wallpaper set bundled with iOS 11, echoing Apple's original 1977 rainbow logo with colorful striped patterns.

title: iOS 11 Space
description: "Space" is one of iOS 11's built-in stock wallpaper categories, featuring imagery of planets, nebulae, and starfields for the Lock Screen and Home Screen.

title: Samsung Galaxy S8
description: Announced March 29, 2017, and released April 21, the Galaxy S8 introduced Samsung's edge-to-edge "Infinity Display" and debuted the Bixby voice assistant.

title: iOS 10
description: Announced at WWDC on June 13, 2016, and released September 13, 2016, iOS 10 redesigned the Lock Screen with interactive widgets and introduced "Raise to Wake."

title: iOS 9
description: Announced at WWDC on June 8, 2015, and released September 16, 2015, iOS 9 brought Split View multitasking to iPad and laid the groundwork for later battery-saving features.

title: iOS 9 beta
description: The iOS 9 developer beta was released June 8, 2015, right after its WWDC announcement, giving developers early access to test the update months ahead of its public release.

title: Mac OS X 10.0 Cheetah
description: Mac OS X 10.0, codenamed Cheetah, was first shown in its near-final form by Steve Jobs at Macworld San Francisco on January 9, 2001, ahead of its retail release on March 24, 2001. It introduced the Aqua interface with its now-iconic Dock, replacing the classic Mac OS after nearly two decades. Despite its groundbreaking design, Cheetah was criticized at launch for being slow and lacking software support.

title: Mac OS X 10.1 Puma
description: Mac OS X 10.1, codenamed Puma, was previewed by Steve Jobs at the Macworld Expo keynote on July 18, 2001, roughly four months after Mac OS X's initial release. It arrived as a free update on September 25, 2001, significantly improving speed, adding DVD playback support, and expanding hardware compatibility. Puma is often considered the release that made Mac OS X practical for everyday use.

title: Mac OS X 10.2 Jaguar
description: Mac OS X 10.2, codenamed Jaguar, was unveiled at WWDC on May 6, 2002, ahead of its release on August 23, 2002. It was the first version to use its big-cat codename in official marketing, introducing Quartz Extreme for hardware-accelerated graphics along with the debut of iChat and Address Book. Jaguar brought major stability and speed improvements over earlier releases.

title: Mac OS X 10.3 Panther
description: Mac OS X 10.3, codenamed Panther, was previewed by Steve Jobs on June 23, 2003, with over 100 new features, ahead of its release on October 24, 2003. It brought a visual refresh with a brushed-metal Finder redesign, along with Exposé for managing open windows and Fast User Switching for multiple accounts. Panther was praised for its noticeable performance gains across the system.

title: Mac OS X 10.4 Tiger
description: Mac OS X 10.4, codenamed Tiger, was announced at WWDC on June 28, 2004, nearly a year before its release on April 29, 2005. It introduced Spotlight, Apple's system-wide search feature, along with Dashboard widgets and improved support for the then-new Intel-based Macs later in its lifecycle. Tiger remained in use longer than most versions due to its stability.

title: Mac OS X 10.5 Leopard
description: Mac OS X 10.5, codenamed Leopard, was first previewed at WWDC on August 7, 2006, though its release was delayed and it didn't arrive until October 26, 2007. It introduced Time Machine for automatic backups, Spaces for virtual desktops, and a redesigned Finder. Leopard was also the first version to run natively on both PowerPC and Intel Macs.

title: Mac OS X 10.5 Leopard Server
description: Mac OS X 10.5 Server, the server edition of Leopard, was previewed alongside the standard version at WWDC on August 7, 2006, before both arrived on October 26, 2007. It shared the same visual design and wallpaper as its desktop counterpart while adding tools for managing networks, file sharing, and collaborative services. It was aimed at businesses, schools, and organizations running Apple hardware.

title: Mac OS X 10.6 Snow Leopard
description: Mac OS X 10.6, codenamed Snow Leopard, was announced at WWDC on June 9, 2008, more than a year before it arrived on August 28, 2009. Unlike most releases, it focused on refinement rather than new features, with Apple rewriting much of the operating system's core for better performance, stability, and a smaller storage footprint. It was also the first version sold exclusively as a digital download alongside physical media.

title: Mac OS X 10.7 Lion
description: Mac OS X 10.7, codenamed Lion, was first previewed at Apple's "Back to the Mac" event on October 20, 2010, ahead of its release on July 20, 2011. It brought multi-touch gestures and iOS-inspired design elements to the Mac, introducing Launchpad, Mission Control, and full-screen apps, along with the Mac App Store as a built-in distribution platform. Lion marked Apple's shift toward blending Mac and iOS interaction patterns.

title: OS X 10.8 Mountain Lion
description: OS X 10.8, codenamed Mountain Lion, was first announced on February 16, 2012, ahead of a public release on July 25, 2012 — an unusual move for Apple, which otherwise revealed most macOS updates at WWDC. It deepened iCloud integration and brought iOS-style apps like Notes, Reminders, and Messages to the Mac. Notification Center also made its debut in this release.

title: OS X 10.9 Mavericks
description: OS X 10.9, codenamed Mavericks, was unveiled on June 10, 2013, at WWDC, ahead of its public release on October 22, 2013. It was the first Mac operating system named after a California landmark rather than a big cat, and the first major macOS update offered as a free download. Mavericks focused on battery efficiency with features like App Nap and Timer Coalescing.

title: OS X 10.10 Yosemite
description: OS X 10.10, codenamed Yosemite, was unveiled on June 2, 2014, at WWDC, with a complete visual overhaul that replaced skeuomorphic design with a flatter, more modern look. It introduced Continuity features like Handoff, allowing tasks to move seamlessly between Mac and iOS devices. It arrived publicly on October 16, 2014, and its redesign set the visual direction for macOS for years to come.

title: OS X 10.11 El Capitan
description: OS X 10.11, codenamed El Capitan, was unveiled on June 8, 2015, at WWDC, with an emphasis on performance and stability rather than visual changes. It introduced Split View for using two apps side by side and refined Spotlight and Mission Control. It was released publicly on September 30, 2015, and is often remembered as one of the most dependable macOS releases.

title: macOS 10.12 Sierra
description: macOS 10.12, codenamed Sierra, was announced at WWDC on June 13, 2016, ahead of its release that September. It was the first release to carry the "macOS" name, dropping "OS X" to align with the branding of iOS, watchOS, and tvOS. Sierra introduced Siri on the Mac for the first time, along with Universal Clipboard and Optimized Storage.

title: macOS 10.13 High Sierra
description: macOS 10.13, codenamed High Sierra, was announced at WWDC on June 5, 2017, and released that September. As its name suggests, it focused on refining its predecessor rather than a visual overhaul, quietly switching the Mac's storage format to APFS and adopting Metal 2 for graphics performance. Most of its improvements happened under the hood rather than on the surface.

title: macOS 10.14 Mojave
description: macOS 10.14, codenamed Mojave, was announced at WWDC on June 4, 2018, and released that September. It introduced a system-wide Dark Mode along with Dynamic Desktop, a wallpaper feature that shifts throughout the day to match the time. Mojave also brought several iOS apps, including News, Stocks, and Home, to the Mac for the first time.

title: macOS 10.15 Catalina
description: macOS 10.15, codenamed Catalina, was announced at WWDC on June 3, 2019, and released that October. It replaced iTunes with three separate apps: Music, Podcasts, and TV, and introduced Sidecar, which lets an iPad function as a wireless second display. Catalina was also the last version of macOS to support 32-bit applications.

title: macOS 11 Big Sur
description: macOS 11, codenamed Big Sur, was announced at WWDC on June 22, 2020, and released that November. It marked the biggest visual redesign since Yosemite, and its jump from version 10.15 straight to 11 reflected just how significant Apple considered the update. Big Sur was also the first version of macOS built to run natively on Apple's own M1 Apple Silicon chips.

title: macOS 12 Monterey
description: macOS 12, codenamed Monterey, was announced at WWDC on June 7, 2021, and released that October. It introduced Universal Control, letting a single keyboard and mouse move seamlessly between a Mac and a nearby iPad, along with the Shortcuts app arriving on the Mac for the first time. FaceTime also gained SharePlay for watching and listening together during calls.

title: macOS 13 Ventura
description: macOS 13, codenamed Ventura, was announced at WWDC on June 6, 2022, and released that October. It introduced Stage Manager for organizing windows and apps, along with Continuity Camera, which lets an iPhone act as a high-quality webcam. Ventura also replaced the long-standing System Preferences app with a redesigned System Settings.

title: macOS 14 Sonoma
description: macOS 14, codenamed Sonoma, was announced at WWDC on June 5, 2023, and released that September. It introduced interactive desktop widgets that could be placed directly on the desktop, along with Presenter Overlay for appearing over shared content during video calls. Sonoma also added a set of new screen savers featuring sweeping aerial landscapes.

title: macOS 15 Sequoia
description: macOS 15, codenamed Sequoia, was announced at WWDC on June 10, 2024, and released that September. It introduced iPhone Mirroring, allowing an iPhone to be viewed and controlled directly from a Mac, along with improved window tiling. Sequoia also deepened integration with Apple Intelligence, Apple's suite of AI-powered features.

title: macOS 26 Tahoe
description: macOS 26, codenamed Tahoe, was announced at WWDC on June 9, 2025, and released that September, marking Apple's switch to year-based version numbers across all its platforms. It introduced the Liquid Glass design language, featuring translucent, color-customizable interface elements, along with a significantly upgraded Spotlight search. Tahoe was also the last version of macOS to support Intel-based Macs.

title: macOS 27 Golden Gate
description: macOS 27, codenamed Golden Gate, was announced at WWDC on June 8, 2026, ahead of its release that fall. Named after the strait connecting San Francisco Bay to the Pacific, it is the first version of macOS to drop support for Intel Macs entirely, running exclusively on Apple Silicon. Golden Gate brings AI-powered features more broadly across the system.

title: iPad Air 2020
description: Announced at Apple's "Time Flies" event on September 15, 2020, the fourth-generation iPad Air was the first Apple device to ship with the A14 Bionic chip, arriving before that year's iPhone. It moved Touch ID into the top button and replaced the Lightning port with USB-C, bringing several iPad Pro features to a more affordable model.

title: iPad Air 2022
description: Unveiled at Apple's "Peek Performance" event on March 8, 2022, the fifth-generation iPad Air adopted the M1 chip, the same silicon used in the iPad Pro at the time, along with 5G support. Its front camera was also repositioned to the landscape edge, making video calls more natural when the iPad is propped up horizontally.

title: iPhone SE (2nd generation)
description: Announced on April 15, 2020, the second-generation iPhone SE revived the classic iPhone 8 design while packing the A13 Bionic chip, the same chip used in the iPhone 11. It relied on a single rear camera paired with software-powered Portrait mode, and became Apple's most affordable iPhone at the time.

title: iPadOS 14
description: Announced at WWDC on June 22, 2020, alongside iOS 14, iPadOS 14 introduced redesigned, resizable widgets on the Home Screen and Scribble, which let Apple Pencil handwriting be automatically converted into typed text. It also brought a new, more compact design for incoming calls and Siri, freeing up screen space on the larger iPad display.

title: iPadOS 16
description: Announced at WWDC on June 6, 2022, alongside iOS 16, iPadOS 16 introduced Stage Manager, a new way to organize multiple resizable, overlapping app windows and extend them onto an external display. The Weather app also arrived on iPad for the first time with this release.

title: iPadOS 17
description: Announced at WWDC on June 5, 2023, alongside iOS 17, iPadOS 17 brought interactive widgets to the Home Screen and introduced the Health app to iPad for the first time. PDF tools were also redesigned, adding smarter form-filling and easier annotation.

title: iPadOS 26
description: Announced at WWDC on June 9, 2025, alongside iOS 26, iPadOS 26 introduced the Liquid Glass design language across the system and brought a more desktop-like windowing system, with freely resizable and overlapping app windows. It marked one of the biggest shifts in how multitasking works on iPad.

title: iPadOS 27
description: Announced at WWDC on June 8, 2026, alongside iOS 27, iPadOS 27 carried over the same headline feature as its iPhone counterpart: Siri AI, a rebuilt version of Siri built on generative AI models capable of holding natural, back-and-forth conversations, now adapted for the larger iPad screen.

title: iPadOS 18
description: Announced at WWDC on June 10, 2024, alongside iOS 18, iPadOS 18 brought Apple Intelligence and a redesigned Control Center to iPad, along with a dedicated Calculator app for the first time, complete with Apple Pencil-powered Math Notes.

title: iPadOS 13
description: Announced at WWDC on June 3, 2019, alongside iOS 13, iPadOS 13 marked the first time Apple split its tablet software into a separate operating system with its own name. It introduced a true desktop-class version of Safari, an overhauled Files app, and the ability to run multiple windows of the same app side by side.

title: iPadOS 15
description: Announced at WWDC on June 7, 2021, alongside iOS 15, iPadOS 15 finally brought widgets to the iPad Home Screen and introduced a new multitasking menu, accessible from a button at the top of every app, for quickly opening Split View and Slide Over. It also added Quick Note, letting notes be jotted down from anywhere in the system.
